svg.title: CoSTOS HAT rev A: watchdog, PWM pump output, feedback and readback
svg.desc: Retriggerable monostable watchdog producing WD_OK; the PWM pump output as a transistor chain: two NPN switches in series (PWM and watchdog) drive a PNP to the supply, an NPN pulls the terminal low; series resistor and TVS; pump feedback inputs with pull-up and RC filter; output readback divider.
svg.text: Timeout ≈ R3 · C5 ≈ 3 s (tuned at bring-up). Only rising
edges on B retrigger U3: CoSTOS toggles HEARTBEAT once per
control cycle (1 s), so an edge arrives every 2 s. A line
stuck high or low lets WD_OK drop.
Power-up: R4/C6 hold CLR low; Q then stays low until the
first heartbeat, so nothing runs while the Pi boots.
JP1 forces WD_OK high for bench tests (open by default).
D3 shows U3's state, not the JP1 override.
5 · PWM pump output PUMP1 (transistor chain H3, D22)
Q4 and Q5 in a row are the watchdog AND: Q6 switches the
output to +V_DRV only while PWM1 and WD_OK are both high.
Either switch off: R36 pulls PWM_OFF high, Q6 turns off
and Q7 pulls the terminal actively to 0 V = stop.
R7 holds PWM1 low while the Pi boots. R9 limits a shorted
cable and the brief Q6/Q7 overlap when switching.
1-Wire Lite: R9 100 Ω, D4 SMBJ6.0A, R31 6.8 kΩ (4.1).
D12 shows what leaves the board: off = stop, brighter = faster.
Terminal order = cable colours brown, blue, black.
PUMP2 (n.f.): the same chain, Q8–Q11, R39–R44, R10, R24,
D5, D14, J3, from PWM2 = GPIO19 (pin 35).
Prototype rev A only: the AND gate + TC4427 chain (U4, U6,
C7, C8) as a jumper-selected fallback (4.1); not on the
faded = not fitted in rev A (n.f.)
